To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rural-urban differences exist in familiarity with and concern about large scale livestock production, and that trust of farmers is negatively related to concern about the environmental impacts of livestock production.
Ohioans have little awareness or concern about large-scale animal agriculture, and that trust of farmers and environmental concern are associated with concern about large-scale agriculture.

1) rural and urban residents of Ohio are similarly familiar and concerned about large-scale livestock and poultry operations; 2) greater trust of farmers is related to less concern about large-scale operations; 3) greater environmental concern is related to greater concern about large-scale animal agriculture; and 4) greater perceptions that large-scale livestock and animal production operations are beneficial are related to lower concern about large-scale agriculture.

understanding how social and economic conditions influence the way in which people perceive and respond to the presence of large-scale livestock and poultry production facilities in their local community and region.
